new_public_evidence.source: Lee and Whiteley, Variance estimation in the particle filter
new_public_evidence.result: Particle-filter asymptotic variance decomposes into generation-wise terms and, at fixed cost, the continuous optimum allocates particles proportional to sqrt(v_p/k_p). Their reported outlier-observation example obtained about a factor-40 variance improvement from optimal allocation. Their non-asymptotic estimator is multinomial-resampling specific, so it is not imported unchanged into the stratified implementation.

new_public_evidence.source: Mastrototaro and Olsson, Adaptive online variance estimation in particle filters: the ALVar estimator
new_public_evidence.result: Genealogy can support online asymptotic-variance monitoring with automatically adapted lag and no extra simulation; this motivates a future past-only ancestry diagnostic, but not a theorem transfer to the current stratified setting.

new_public_evidence.source: Flenghi and Jourdain, Central limit theorem for the stratified resampling mechanism
new_public_evidence.result: Provides a direct CLT for stratified resampling. Its recursive particle-filter variance formula relies on a stated later-step conjecture, leaving the rigorous single-run multi-generation stratified variance-estimator bridge open.
Earlier-stage variance observations can guide later-stage allocations with analyzable learning cost, supporting predictable past-only reallocation rather than current-outcome-dependent stopping.

new_public_evidence.source: Hesterberg, Weighted Average Importance Sampling and Defensive Mixture Distributions
new_public_evidence.result: Retaining a nominal/base component is an established protection against proposal misspecification; used here only as a cross-field analogy for a uniform particle reserve.

derived_results.claim: In a five-generation two-state Feynman-Kac model whose shock potential moves one generation per regime, the exact Lee-Whiteley-style relative variance contribution argmax moves 0->1->2->3->4. Exact coefficient vectors were [3.82185,0.12841,0.14383,0.10443,0.03992], [2.34765,2.90649,0.09977,0.09138,0.03825], [1.65202,1.94085,2.36518,0.06526,0.03460], [1.27879,1.43549,1.65942,2.01952,0.02598], and [1.06027,1.14582,1.26489,1.45916,1.78250].

A completed-run plug-in CV^2 of the finite-state continuation value H_p=Q_{p,5}(1), evaluated only after the run and then used for the next schedule, identified the dominant generation in 100%, 85.6%, 85.2%, 83.9% and 83.5% of 3000 uniform-64 runs across the five regimes. Median relative L1 coefficient error ranged from about 1.5% to 12.0%. This is an engineering asymptotic proxy, not a theorem-level stratified genealogy estimator.

For q_p=(1-beta)/5 + beta*sqrt(Abar_p)/sum sqrt(Abar), the separable asymptotic objective has the distribution-free stale-estimate bound V(q;A) <= V_uniform(A)/(1-beta). Thus beta=0.5 gives a 2x mismatch ceiling while preserving directional allocation. In the exact five-regime coefficient stress, beta=0.5 had matched-regime variance ratios 0.576-0.994 of uniform and worst stale cross-regime ratio 1.234; beta=0.75 reached better matched ratios 0.510-0.992 but a worse stale ratio 1.571. An unhedged floor-16 KKT allocator reached 2.289 in the same stale stress.

With independent stratified resampling, total budget 320, beta=0.5 and past-only EWMA alpha=0.6, independent recurring-drift streams gave normalized-MSE reductions versus uniform of 5.0%, 7.2%, 9.7% and 11.9% for regime phase lengths 5, 10, 20 and 50 runs respectively. The phase-5 paired result was directionally positive but weak (t about 1.81); phase 10/20/50 had paired t about 4.08/7.27/11.27. At phase length 20 the schedule argmax caught the new dominant generation in median 2 runs, q90 4.

The more aggressive floor-constrained KKT controller, driven by the same lagged proxy, was about 14.9% worse than uniform at phase length 5, roughly neutral at 10, and about 6.6% better at 20. The fast-drift failure is therefore stale-coefficient sensitivity rather than a failure of the square-root allocation principle itself.

For V=sum A_p/N_p and variable budget B=sum k_p N_p, the optimum is N_p=B sqrt(A_p/k_p)/S with S=sum sqrt(A_p k_p), yielding V*=S^2/B. Adding fixed per-run overhead C0 makes idealized confirmation compute proportional to S^2(1+C0/B). Hence extra descendants only amortize fixed overhead after the within-run optimum: stop increasing B when C0/B is below the tolerated overhead fraction epsilon, equivalently B>=C0/epsilon; the maximum remaining latency gain from infinite B is C0/(B+C0).

A theorem-clean single-run generation-wise variance estimator for the current independent-stratified multi-generation implementation was not established. Lee-Whiteley's exact finite-N genealogy estimator is multinomial-specific; the identified stratified CLT does not by itself close the full recursive estimator. This gap is preserved rather than silently importing multinomial guarantees.

engineering_update.scope: Synthetic five-generation recurring-drift Feynman-Kac evaluation plus analytic defensive-allocation and fixed-overhead rules. Numeric gains are model-specific; theorem claims are restricted to the separable asymptotic allocation algebra and predictable scheduling.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The continuation-value proxy uses exact finite-state H=Q_{p,5}(1); real agent evaluation would need an estimated influence/continuation proxy.
No theorem-level unbiased or consistent finite-N stratified genealogy estimator was claimed from the multinomial Lee-Whiteley construction.
The Flenghi-Jourdain recursive particle-filter variance extension is not treated as fully proved because the paper states a later-step conjectural condition.
The 2x beta=0.5 mismatch ceiling applies to the separable asymptotic objective sum A_p/N_p, not arbitrary finite-N particle filters.
Phase-length-5 improvement is not reported as statistically decisive in the finite validation used here.
Current-run outcome-dependent particle stopping remains outside the predictable-count correctness argument.
No AGI capability or real-agent performance claim follows from this synthetic model.
frontier: Build a 10-20 generation moving-shock model and compare the continuation-value CV^2 proxy with an ALVar-style lagged ancestry dispersion diagnostic; treat the latter as heuristic under stratified resampling until a theorem is found.

Replace fixed beta=0.5 with a predictable uncertainty-aware hedge: choose the largest beta whose coefficient uncertainty set satisfies a prespecified worst-case variance-inflation cap, and only concentrate after stability is certified.

Search for a rigorous single-run generation-wise variance estimator compatible with independent stratified resampling; otherwise explicitly separate a multinomial diagnostic estimator from stratified production and quantify the estimator/resampling mismatch.

Extend the fixed-overhead allocation to random tool costs and parallel descendants using N_p proportional to sqrt(A_p/k_p) with past-only cost estimates; optimize confirmation latency, not sample variance alone.
Map to multi-turn agent trajectories only after base/proposal transition likelihoods, high-fidelity label semantics, and a computable per-generation influence proxy are explicit.
exact_next_action: Construct a 10-20 generation moving-shock model and implement two past-only diagnostics side by side: the continuation-value CV^2 proxy and an ALVar-style lagged ancestry dispersion statistic computed from the same independent-stratified cloud but treated as heuristic until a stratified theorem is established. Maintain an uncertainty set for the generation-wise coefficient vector and select beta predictably as the largest concentration level satisfying a chosen worst-case variance-inflation cap. Compare abrupt, gradual and recurring drift on adaptation lag, normalized MSE and fixed-overhead confirmation latency. In parallel continue the public-source search for a rigorous stratified single-run variance estimator; do not import multinomial genealogy guarantees unchanged.
